messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered - backend.p99 latency breach (service: inference-cache) at 12:04 UTC. count=27, p99=1.8s, p95=620ms
Leah S: saw this, getting pages. investigating cache tier.
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident #INC-4652 triggered, routing to oncall: @Ravi K.
Ravi K: on it — I'm looking at current deploys and recent autoscaler events.
Marta P: FYI we had a small config push to cache scaling at 11:58, could be related.
Nikhil: seeing a spike in cache evictions in metrics: eviction_rate jumped x8 at 11:59. probe shows many short-lived keys.
Leah S: timeline matches. eviction surge -> more origin hits -> tail latency up. is the LRU thrashing?
Ravi K: running quick checks, attaching logs:
```
# kubectl logs -n inference inference-cache-7f9d -c cache-engine | tail -n 80
2026-03-14T11:59:43Z [warn] eviction: freed 1200 keys
2026-03-14T12:00:01Z [info] mem_used=78% threshold=65%
2026-03-14T12:01:05Z [error] perf: loopback miss spike
```
```
Ravi K: mem usage climbed after that config push, looks like promo burst + smaller cache size due to new default ttl.
Leah S: ok. for mitigation: can we temporarily increase cache size on the hot pool and reduce churn?
Nikhil: yes, we can bump pool size and revert the ttl change. doing `kubectl patch` now.
Marta P: heads-up — increasing pool will move memory between nodes, could trigger OOM if not careful. watch eviction graphs.
Ravi K: I'm going to ack noisy latency alerts and silence the lower-priority p95 alerts while we mitigate — want to avoid paging for expected recovery noise.
Leah S: agree. Please document the silence window and which alerts.
Ravi K: executed: `/alerts silence --selector service:inference-cache,severity:warning --until 2026-03-14T13:30:00Z --comment "temporary while we mitigate eviction thrash"`
ops-bot: Action logged: alerts.silence by Ravi K — selector=service:inference-cache,severity:warning until=2026-03-14T13:30:00Z
Leah S: can we surface a quick dashboard panel for eviction_rate + p99 so AG (product) can see impact?
Marta P: created a dashboard panel: "cache: eviction_rate / tail_latency" and linked to incident: <https://dashboards.redwood.company/d/xyz/cache-eviction-live>
Nikhil: after bumping pool and reverting ttl we see eviction_rate down to baseline in ~3m and p99 trending back under 400ms.
Ravi K: good. I'll keep an eye on autoscaler and scheduler churn. Are we confident this is config-induced and not mem leak?
Leah S: logs point to eviction churn rather than leak. set follow-up to run heap check but not blocking.
Marta P: customer impact check: only a small subset of requests hit the affected hot pool; no major customer-facing errors recorded. ticketing flag set to LOW_IMPACT.
Leah S: ok. next: post-incident alert tuning — the p95 alarm is too sensitive during small eviction spikes, propose: raise p95 threshold from 500ms -> 700ms and tie paging to sustained breach 5m->3min? (i.e., only page if p95>700ms for 3m).
Ravi K: proposal sounds reasonable. also suggest adding eviction_rate metric as an alert input so we don't page on transient tail if eviction_rate==high. e.g., `if p95>700ms AND eviction_rate>200/s for 2m`
Nikhil: will draft the new alert rule config. snippet:
```
- alert: inference_cache_tail_latency
  expr: p95_latency > 0.7 and eviction_rate > 200
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: critical
```

Leah S: add a regression test in the alerting CI to exercise simulated eviction bursts so we can validate changes before rollout.
Marta P: noted. I'll create a ticket and assign to eng-alerting.
Ravi K: starting handoff — I'm going to sign out in 10 but leaving ops notes and runbook link: <https://runbooks.redwood.company/cache-eviction>. Please confirm final steps.
Leah S: steps for post-incident cleanup:
- remove temporary silence after validation (do not auto-expire if we still see noise)
- roll alert rule change in staging -> verify with chaos test
- add maintenance window for next deploy so this config change doesn't retrigger alerts
- update runbook with TTL default and pool sizing notes
- close incident and tag customers as LOW_IMPACT if no downstream errors

Ravi K: marking tasks in incident compass and assigning: Marta (dashboard + maintenance window), Nikhil (alert rule + CI test), Leah (runbook + customer comms).
Leah S: post-incident check in: schedule 24h re-eval on metric baselines and a 72h follow-up to ensure thresholds are correct.
ops-bot: Note: silence expires at 2026-03-14T13:30:00Z unless updated.
Marta P: I will remove the silence once we confirm eviction_rate stays low for 60m.
Nikhil: pushed alert rule draft to `alerting/patches/1862-cache-eviction.yml`, requesting review from @Leah S.
Leah S: reviewed, left comments about `for: 3m` -> change to 4m in staging to reduce flapping, ok with 3m in prod after CI.
Ravi K: handing off oncall to @Marta P now. I'm out. :wave: good ops everyone.
Marta P: taking over. will monitor for 1 hour and then clear temporary artifacts.
Leah S: thanks all — filing the postmortem and action items now. follow-up checklist in ticket INC-4652. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident INC-4652 resolved (status: mitigated) at 12:38 UTC.
Marta P: post-incident cleanup TODO (short list):
- remove `/alerts silence` entry after 60m stable
- merge alert rule after CI and schedule staged rollout
- add 2 dashboard widgets (evictions p10/p95, memory headroom)
- update runbook section "cache sizing" with the new default ttl note

Leah S: I'll validate thresholds tomorrow morning during the low-traffic window and confirm here before we close the incident fully.
Marta P: will also create maintenance window for next config deploy to avoid noise.
Nikhil: adding a synthetic test to trigger eviction pattern and verify page/no-page logic. will link results. :eyes:
